description: Cross-language numerical conformance reference for sce_forge_runtime generated code. All five languages (C++, Rust, Python, Kotlin, Go) MUST produce these exact outputs. Every entry is computed by hand from the algorithms in sce-forge-runtime/rust/src/ and verified against the live Rust smoke tests. If any language disagrees, the bug is in that language's codegen template or runtime helper — not in this file.
expected_shape: For fixtures with a single output, 'expected' is a scalar (number or bool). For compound-output fixtures (procedures returning ProcedureResult, transforms with multiple <data direction=out>), 'expected' is a JSON object whose keys are the SCXML data ids in snake_case. Each language test must map those canonical keys to its own identifier case (camelCase / PascalCase / snake_case). A case of an algorithm that declares may-fail (SCE_FORGE.md §3.4.1) may carry 'fails' — the failure's contract name ('overflow', 'divide-by-zero', 'capacity-exceeded') — in place of 'expected'.

crossfile_procedure_codec.description: Procedure with an <sce:import kind=codec> member. The sendRequest state emits <send sce:payload='frame.encode()'>, dispatching the codec's 4-byte encoding through the service handler. Frame is default-initialized by the generated procedure ctor, so encode() returns [0, 0, 0, 0]. Loud-failing on drift proves that cross-file codec member calls are wired into the procedure's payload capture path end-to-end across all five languages.

cases.note: default-initialized frame emits zero bytes; no codec-state mutation path yet

crossfile_procedure_filter.description: Procedure imports a stateful filter and dispatches the filter's update() method via <assign location='smoothed' expr='smoother.update(rawSample)'/>. Verifies that cross-file member-method calls on a non-codec stateful kind route through the same expression pipeline as codec.encode() across all six backends. Filter return is a primitive (float64) so the C11 lowering calls `<snake>_update(&_st->member, ...)` directly — no wrapper conversion is needed because there is no codec-style payload contract to bridge. The expected outcome is that the procedure reaches the `done` final state regardless of the raw sample value; numerical correctness of the filter itself is exercised by the standalone `filter_low_pass` fixture, so this case validates the cross-file dispatch wiring rather than the filter math.

cases.note: first sample — fresh filter passes through warm-up

crossfile_procedure_codec_mutate.description: Procedure that imports a codec, mutates one field via <assign location='frame.msgId' expr='msgId'/>, then dispatches frame.encode() through the service handler. Proves end-to-end that the unified LHS pipeline + stateful_import_field_renames correctly wire dotted member assignment into codec mutation across all five languages.

cases.note: frame.msgId = 42 -> encode -> [42, 0, 0, 0]; length and payload remain default-zero

procedure_security_access.description: UDS Security Access flow with a first-class <sce:helper name='computeKey'> DI injection point. The generator emits computeKey as a typed closure member + setter on the generated state machine (mirroring serviceHandler); the conformance harness passes in a deterministic stub (XOR each byte with 0xA5) as an additional execute() wrapper argument across all 5 languages. The handler's response data is 'SEED' on every call, so the RequestSeed -> SendKey transition's <assign location='seed' expr='_event.data'/> populates seed with the 4 bytes [0x53, 0x45, 0x45, 0x44]; SendKey then dispatches computeKey(seed) = [0xF6, 0xE0, 0xE0, 0xE1] through the capture channel. Verifies end-to-end: multi-state multi-send, transition-assign from _event.data, guarded eventless transitions (retry loop structurally emitted but not exercised in the happy path), and the helper-DI wiring proving the framework's first-class solution to the 'user-provided expression helpers' escape hatch.

cases.note: happy path: handler returns 'SEED' (0x53,0x45,0x45,0x44) on every call -> seed assigned on RequestSeed edge -> SendKey dispatches computeKey stub output (XOR 0xA5) = [0xF6,0xE0,0xE0,0xE1] = [246,224,224,225]

codec_cbor_map.description: SCE_FORGE.md §4.6.1: an integer-keyed CBOR map written in RFC 8949's deterministic encoding — keys ascending, shortest heads — with an optional entry written only when present. `null` in a case is an absent optional entry. id = 00 01 … 0f, source = "node-a" (6e 6f 64 65 2d 61), payload = de ad.

cases.note: five entries (0xa5); the absent deadline is not written
deadline 2^32 needs the 8-byte head (0x1b), and key 12 follows key 7
a present false and a present zero are written, and are not absence

rejects.why: the required pattern entry (key 3) is absent from a four-entry map
the id is fifteen bytes where its declared length is sixteen
a text string where the urgent entry expects a truth value
an indefinite-length map, which the codec never reads

codec_zenoh_ext_envelope.signature: (raw: &[u8]) -> {header_flags: u8 @ byte 0, extensions: tlv-chain<codec_zenoh_ext_entry> max-depth=8 on-overflow=reject terminate-on=entry-flag(Z)}
codec_zenoh_ext_envelope.description: Decode-rejection vectors only. The chain's entries are typed sub-codecs, so the field shape is not expressible as StructField and the fixture stays oracle_eligible=false for round-trip cases -- but what a chain refuses needs no field values to pin. Entries here are unit extensions, one byte each: ext_id in bits 0..3, enc=0 in bits 5..6, Z (another entry follows) in bit 7.

rejects.why: chain saturates max-depth=8 with the entry flag still set, so the ninth entry the peer sent is refused rather than dropped
the last entry declares a successor and the frame ends there, so the chain is short rather than finished

codec_zenoh_msg_put.signature: (raw: &[u8]) -> {header: u8 flags @ byte 0, timestamp: T-gated embed, encoding: E-gated embed, extensions: Z-gated tlv-chain<codec_zenoh_ext_entry> max-depth=8 on-overflow=reject terminate-on=entry-flag(Z), payload_len: vle u64, payload: bytes}
codec_zenoh_msg_put.description: Decode-rejection vectors only (see codec_zenoh_ext_envelope). This is the present-if-gated chain, and the chain is followed on the wire by payload_len + payload -- which is what makes a refused entry a corruption rather than a loss: dropping it silently leaves its header byte under the cursor, where payload_len then reads it. Header 0x81 = MID 0x01 with Z set, T and E clear.

rejects.why: nine extensions on a max-depth=8 chain: the ninth entry's header byte must not be read as payload_len

codec_little_endian.signature: (raw: &[u8]) <-> {sensorId: u8 @ byte 0, value: u16 @ byte 1 little-endian, status: u8 @ byte 3}
codec_little_endian.description: Multi-field little-endian frame. Encode emits [sensorId, value_lo, value_hi, status]; decode reverses. Field names use SCXML source case (camelCase) as the canonical oracle key; each language fragment applies its own case filter to match the generated struct's native naming.

codec_simple_frame.signature: (raw: &[u8]) <-> {msgId: u8 @ byte 0, length: u8 @ byte 1, payload: u16 @ byte 2 big-endian}
codec_simple_frame.description: Big-endian 4-byte frame. Encode emits [msgId, length, payload_hi, payload_lo]; decode reverses. Byte-order contrast to codec_little_endian proves the encode/decode expressions track sce:default-endian.

codec_subbyte.signature: (raw: &[u8]) <-> {priority: u8 @ byte 0 bits[7:5], channel: u8 @ byte 0 bits[4:2], direction: u8 @ byte 0 bits[1:0]}
codec_subbyte.description: Sub-byte bit-field extraction packed into a single byte: priority(3b) | channel(3b) | direction(2b). Encode shifts and ORs; decode shifts and masks. Exercises the sub-byte branch of the codec code generator which produces different expressions from whole-byte fields.

codec_tail.signature: (raw: &[u8]) <-> {msgId: u8 @ byte 0, status: u8 @ byte 1, payload: bytes @ byte 2 tail (max 32)}
codec_tail.description: Variable-length tail payload codec (sce:bit-size="tail"). Bytes 0 and 1 carry msgId + status; everything from byte 2 onward is the raw payload up to the end of the frame. Encode appends the payload after the 2-byte header; decode slices from byte 2 to the buffer end. Exercises the BitSize::Tail arm and the V5 builder-pattern encode lift across all six backends.

codec_length_ref.signature: (raw: &[u8]) <-> {msgId: u8 @ byte 0, len: u8 @ byte 1, payload: bytes @ byte 2 length-ref:len (max 32)}
codec_length_ref.description: Length-prefixed payload codec (sce:bit-size="length-ref" + sce:length-field="len"). The byte at offset 1 explicitly states the payload length, so decode reads exactly len bytes starting at byte 2. Each oracle case keeps len consistent with payload.length so the round-trip exercises both directions without corrupting the length field. Closes the second of two BitSize variants left unimplemented in the c11 codec emitter.

codec_vle_zint_u64.signature: base-128 LSB-first VLE (canonical Zenoh ZInt); bit 7 = continuation except the final byte carries 8 data bits — u64 caps at 9 bytes

cases.note: 2^56: first 9-byte value (8 continuation bytes + 1 data bit in the 9th)
2^63 - 1: last value whose 9th byte fits 7 bits (bit 7 clear)
2^63: first value with bit 63 set — 9th byte reuses bit 7 as data (was 10 bytes pre-cap)
u64::MAX → 9 bytes (canonical Zenoh ZInt cap; 10 bytes would desync zenoh/zenoh-pico)

codec_zenoh_close.description: Zenoh transport-layer Close body (RFC §5.B B5-prep). Single uint8 reason code; the 1-byte transport-message header (MID + flags) is written separately by `_z_transport_message_encode` so this body codec covers the reason byte alone. Pure composition of B1 Fixed bit-size — no new IR/parser/template surface. Upstream parity: `_z_close_encode` in zenoh-pico src/protocol/codec/transport.c:335-343.

codec_zenoh_frame.signature: (raw: &[u8]) <-> {sn: u64 VLE @ byte 0, payload: bytes tail @ byte 1 (max 65536)}
codec_zenoh_frame.description: Zenoh transport-layer Frame body (RFC §5.B B5-prep). VLE-encoded sequence number followed by a tail-bytes payload consumed to the end of the Frame slice. Applied combination of B1-α VLE primitive + B1 tail bit-size. The transport-message header byte and the `_Z_FLAG_T_Z` extension-chain branch (rejected upstream for Frame) are out of scope. Upstream parity: `_z_frame_encode` in zenoh-pico src/protocol/codec/transport.c:386-395.

codec_qos_byte.signature: (raw: &[u8]) <-> {qos: u8 @ byte 0 with priority:3 + reliable:1 + congestion:2 + express:1 + reserved:1}
codec_qos_byte.description: Multi-bit flag accessor synthetic (RFC §5.B B5-α). The wire shape is a plain uint8 — the bit-range subdivision lives entirely in the accessor surface (priority @ bits 0..2, reliable @ bit 3, congestion @ bits 4..5, express @ bit 6, reserved @ bit 7). Round-trip cases verify that the carrier byte travels through encode/decode unchanged regardless of which sub-ranges are set; per-language accessor tests (priority(), set_priority(), ...) live in each backend's smoke harness rather than here. Mirrors zenoh-pico `_z_n_qos_t._val` (zenoh-pico/include/zenoh-pico/protocol/core.h).

cases.note: all bit-ranges clear (priority=0, reliable=false, congestion=0, express=false, reserved=false)
all bit-ranges max (priority=7, reliable=true, congestion=3, express=true, reserved=true)

codec_zenoh_locator.signature: (raw: &[u8]) <-> {locator_len: u64 VLE @ byte 0, locator: utf-8 string length-ref @ byte 1 (max 128)}
codec_zenoh_locator.description: Zenoh single-locator body (RFC §5.B B5-ζ Surface H). VLE-encoded length prefix + length-ref UTF-8 string payload. First reachable consumer for `sce:type="string"` codec emit — wire shape mirrors zenoh-pico `_z_string_encode`/`_z_string_decode` (codec.c:324-343), but the host language emits `String` / `std::string` / `kotlin.String` / `string` / `str` instead of the byte container. Decode validates UTF-8 and surfaces typed `CodecError::InvalidUtf8` (Rust / Go / Python) or the truncation sentinel (Cpp / Kotlin). Encode trusts the host string invariant.

cases.note: ASCII Zenoh locator URL (18 bytes UTF-8)
Latin-1 é encoded as 2-byte UTF-8 0xC3 0xA9 (locator_len counts UTF-8 bytes, not codepoints)

codec_zenoh_keep_alive.description: Zenoh transport-layer KeepAlive body (RFC §5.B B5-α empty-codec lift). The 1-byte transport-message header (MID + flags) marks the message; the body codec emits zero wire bytes. Empty round-trip case confirms encode produces an empty byte sequence and decode advances the cursor by 0 bytes regardless of remaining input. Upstream parity: `_z_keep_alive_encode` in zenoh-pico src/protocol/codec/transport.c.

cases.note: empty body — encode/decode round-trips zero bytes

codec_zenoh_put.description: Stripped-down Zenoh PUT body leaf (RFC §5.B B5-η Surface I, recursive variant body). Used as the PUT-arm body inside the inner variant codec_zenoh_push_body, which is in turn an arm body of the outer variant codec_zenoh_push — that nesting is what Surface I validates. Upstream `_z_msg_put_t` carries encoding + commons (timestamp + source_info) + attachment + payload, most flag-gated by the parent header (B5-γ parent-flags territory). The fixture keeps a single fixed-byte payload so the recursion focus is not blurred by orthogonal Surface C plumbing.

codec_zenoh_del.description: Stripped-down Zenoh DEL body leaf (RFC §5.B B5-η Surface I, recursive variant body). Used as the DEL-arm body inside the inner variant codec_zenoh_push_body. Empty body — the inner variant's header byte (carrying the DEL MID) marks the message and the body codec emits zero wire bytes, exactly the pattern codec_zenoh_keep_alive (B5-α) established. The DEL/empty + PUT/non-empty asymmetry on the inner variant arms exercises both empty-body and non-empty-body branches through the recursion path. Upstream `_z_msg_del_t` carries timestamp + source_info both flag-gated by the parent header — modelling that faithfully would require B5-γ parent-flags.

cases.note: empty body — encode/decode round-trips zero bytes

codec_zenoh_fragment.signature: (raw: &[u8]) <-> {sn: u64 VLE @ byte 0, payload: bytes tail @ byte 1 (max 65536)}
codec_zenoh_fragment.description: Zenoh transport-layer Fragment body (RFC §5.B B5-ι). VLE-encoded sequence number followed by tail-bytes payload — same wire shape as codec_zenoh_frame (the MID and host-level reliability/more-fragments semantics differ but the body bytes do not). With Z=0 (no extensions) the encode/decode is a textbook VLE-then-tail. Pure composition of B1-α VLE + B1 tail. Upstream parity: `_z_fragment_encode` in zenoh-pico src/protocol/codec/transport.c:409-434, no-extension fast path lines 429-431.

codec_zenoh_decl_final.description: Zenoh declare-final body (RFC §5.B B5-ι). Empty body — the enclosing declaration header byte carries the DeclFinal sub-variant tag and the body codec emits zero wire bytes. DeclFinal is one of nine `_z_declaration_t` sub-variants (Decl/UndeclKeyExpr, Decl/UndeclSubscriber, Decl/UndeclQueryable, Decl/UndeclToken plus DeclFinal). Upstream parity: `_z_decl_final_t` in zenoh-pico include/zenoh-pico/protocol/definitions/declarations.h:81-86 — placeholder bool kept for future-proofing; wire body is empty.

cases.note: empty body — encode/decode round-trips zero bytes

codec_length_ref_dotted_basic.signature: (raw: &[u8]) <-> {carrier: u8 flags @ byte 0 (hdr:4 + payload_len:4), payload: bytes length-ref @ byte 1 (length = carrier.payload_len, max 15)}
codec_length_ref_dotted_basic.description: RFC §5.B B5-κ Surface L primitive demo — `sce:length-field="<carrier>.<flag>"` dotted-path. Length of the bytes payload is sourced from a multi-bit flag subfield (`carrier.payload_len`, width=4 at bit 4) inside the flags-bearing carrier rather than a separate sibling integer field. Mirrors B1-δ present-if's dotted-path grammar exactly (same syntax, different operation: length-extract instead of bit-test). First reachable consumer is codec_zenoh_scout where the upstream zenoh-pico wire packs `zid_len_m1` into `cbyte[4..7]`.

cases.note: carrier=0x21 (hdr=1, payload_len=2 in high nibble) — 2-byte payload
carrier=0xF5 (hdr=5, payload_len=15 = max for 4-bit width) — 15-byte payload

lookup_engine_status.description: Engine status code to status enum. Input is a uint8 diagnostic status byte; output is one of {STOP, RUNNING, FAULT}. Default miss policy returns STOP for any unrecognized input.

enum_uds_nrc.description: A UDS negative-response-code vocabulary. What six languages must agree on is the NUMBER each variant carries, because that number is on a wire; the SPELLING legitimately differs (GeneralReject in C++/Rust/Go, GENERAL_REJECT in Python/Kotlin), so the key is the source name the document writes and each fragment applies its own case filter. Values are non-consecutive and do not start at zero on purpose: a conversion that dropped them and let the language assign ordinals would produce 0..4 and pass any check comparing only variant count or order.

pattern_kind.description: The Mesh envelope's pattern (SCE_MESH.md §13, key 3), from sce:std/mesh/pattern_kind.scxml. The numbers are the wire's; 10-13 are reserved for the Stream patterns and must not appear, so a conversion that assigned ordinals would give 17 consecutive values and fail here.

payload_codec.description: The Mesh envelope's datacontenttype (SCE_MESH.md §13, key 4), from sce:std/mesh/payload_codec.scxml.

rpc_status.description: The Mesh envelope's rpc_status (SCE_MESH.md §13, key 10), from sce:std/mesh/rpc_status.scxml: the gRPC status codes the Mesh uses, with the holes of the codes it does not.

timer_tester_present.description: A keepalive: <sce:period>2s</sce:period>, fires TesterPresent, reset on DiagRequestSent, cancelled on leaving SessionActive. The oracle is the sequence of calls the generated class makes on the INJECTED timer, recorded by a mock, plus the handler call a firing is routed to. That surface is common to all six language arms, which is what lets one oracle serve them all.

sequence.note: the recorded callback routes to the handler
<sce:reset-on> is cancel THEN start, in that order
<sce:cancel-on state-exit> cancels and does not re-arm

event_schema_sensor_sample.signature: struct EventSchemaSensorSamplePayload { uint16 sensorId; int32 reading; uint8 status; }
event_schema_sensor_sample.description: An event schema emits a payload STRUCT and no behaviour, so what six languages must agree on is the SHAPE: the field names, their ORDER, and that a value written to a field reads back unchanged. It is deliberately NOT a width claim — the same uint8 is uint8_t in C++, u8 in Rust and a plain int in Python's dataclass, so a boundary value would wrap in some arms and not others and the fixture would fail for a difference this kind never promised to remove. Every value here is in range for every arm. Three fields rather than one because ORDER and COUNT are not observable with a single field; `reading` is negative on purpose, so a signed field rendered unsigned cannot pass.

event_schema_hlc.signature: struct EventSchemaHlcPayload { int64 wallTime; uint32 counter; uint64 nodeId; }
event_schema_hlc.description: A hybrid logical clock stamp, the record type the algorithm fixtures algorithm_hlc_compare and algorithm_hlc_tick take and return (SCE_FORGE.md §4.12). A SHAPE claim like every event-schema fixture: names, order, and that a value reads back. The field ids are camelCase so the Rust and Go arms, which respell them, are exercised.

hlc_timestamp.signature: struct HlcTimestampPayload { int64 wallTime; uint32 counter; uint64 nodeId; }
hlc_timestamp.description: A hybrid logical clock timestamp, the record type the standard documents sce:std/merge/hlc_send, hlc_receive and hlc_compare take and return (SCE_FORGE.md §4.12). A SHAPE claim like every event-schema fixture: names, order, and that a value reads back.

orset_entry.signature: struct OrsetEntryPayload { uint64 element; int64 wallTime; uint32 counter; uint64 nodeId; }
orset_entry.description: One entry of an observed-remove set — an element and the hybrid logical clock tag of the add that put it there — the element type of the lists the standard documents sce:std/merge/orset_* take and return (SCE_FORGE.md §4.12). A SHAPE claim like every event-schema fixture: names, order, and that a value reads back.

envelope_id.signature: struct EnvelopeIdPayload { uint64 hi; uint64 lo; }
envelope_id.description: A 16-byte Mesh envelope identifier as its two big-endian halves, the element type of the duplicate-suppression window the standard documents sce:std/mesh/dedup_* take and return (SCE_FORGE.md §4.12). A SHAPE claim like every event-schema fixture: names, order, and that a value reads back.

ordering_slot.signature: struct OrderingSlotPayload { uint64 seq; int64 arrivedAtMs; }
ordering_slot.description: One envelope a Mesh receiver holds back until its sender's sequence reaches it, as its sequence and arrival time, the element type of the lists the standard documents sce:std/mesh/ordering_* take and return (SCE_FORGE.md §4.12). A SHAPE claim like every event-schema fixture: names, order, and that a value reads back.

civil_date.signature: struct CivilDatePayload { int32 year; uint8 month; uint8 day; }
civil_date.description: A proleptic Gregorian date, the record type the standard document sce:std/time/civil_from_days.scxml returns (SCE_FORGE.md §4.12). A SHAPE claim like every event-schema fixture: names, order, and that a value reads back.

merkle_node.signature: struct MerkleNodePayload { uint8 depth; uint64 prefix; uint32 hash; }
merkle_node.description: One node of a merkle digest over timestamped changes — its depth, its base-3 minute prefix, and the XOR of the hashes under it — the element type of the digests the standard documents sce:std/merge/merkle_* take and return (SCE_FORGE.md §4.12). A SHAPE claim like every event-schema fixture: names, order, and that a value reads back.

merkle_divergence.signature: struct MerkleDivergencePayload { bool differs; int64 millis; }
merkle_divergence.description: What the standard document sce:std/merge/merkle_diff.scxml finds between two digests: whether they differ, and the minute boundary from which to exchange changes (SCE_FORGE.md §4.12). A SHAPE claim like every event-schema fixture: names, order, and that a value reads back.

change_entry.signature: struct ChangeEntryPayload { uint64 item; uint8 op; uint64 token; }
change_entry.description: One row of a collection's change log — the item, 1 added / 2 modified / 3 deleted, and the sync token of the change — the element type of the log the standard document sce:std/sync/changes_since.scxml takes and returns (SCE_FORGE.md §4.12). A SHAPE claim like every event-schema fixture: names, order, and that a value reads back.

gcra_decision.signature: struct GcraDecisionPayload { bool admitted; int64 tat; int64 retryAfter; }
gcra_decision.description: A rate limiter's decision — admitted, the theoretical arrival time to keep, and the wait of a refused request — the record type the standard document sce:std/rate/gcra_admit.scxml returns (SCE_FORGE.md §4.12). A SHAPE claim like every event-schema fixture: names, order, and that a value reads back.

mailbox_slot.signature: struct MailboxSlotPayload { int64 id; uint64 hi; uint64 lo; }
mailbox_slot.description: One message waiting in a device's mailbox — the id the mailbox gave it and the sender's 16-byte message id as two big-endian halves — the element type of the queue the standard documents sce:std/sync/mailbox_*.scxml take and return (SCE_FORGE.md §4.12). A SHAPE claim like every event-schema fixture: names, order, and that a value reads back.

acl_privilege.signature: struct AclPrivilegePayload { uint32 id; uint32 parent; }
acl_privilege.description: One privilege of a supported-privilege tree and the aggregate that contains it — the element type of the tree the standard document sce:std/acl/acl_granted.scxml takes (SCE_FORGE.md §4.12). A SHAPE claim like every event-schema fixture: names, order, and that a value reads back.

acl_ace.signature: struct AclAcePayload { uint32 principal; uint32 privilege; }
acl_ace.description: One grant of an access control list — a principal, or a pseudo-principal at the top of the range, and the privilege it is granted — the element type of the list the standard document sce:std/acl/acl_granted.scxml takes (SCE_FORGE.md §4.12). A SHAPE claim like every event-schema fixture: names, order, and that a value reads back.

acl_edge.signature: struct AclEdgePayload { uint32 member; uint32 group; }
acl_edge.description: One membership — a principal and a group it belongs to — the element type of the graph the standard document sce:std/acl/acl_membership.scxml walks (SCE_FORGE.md §4.12). A SHAPE claim like every event-schema fixture: names, order, and that a value reads back.

item_version.signature: struct ItemVersionPayload { uint64 item; uint64 token; }
item_version.description: One item a replica holds and the sync token of the change that last wrote it — the element of the state the standard document sce:std/sync/changes_apply.scxml takes and returns (SCE_FORGE.md §4.12). A SHAPE claim like every event-schema fixture: names, order, and that a value reads back.
